formal_entries.label: qu:i-good-no-bmp
formal_entries.text:
\label{qu:i-good-no-bmp}
Extend the complete topology of \cref{thm:positive-model-complete-metric} to ordinary models of zero lower volume and beyond bounded mass, retaining analytic closure exactly at the ideal models. Recover the curve topology of \cref{cor:curve-model-completeness} and the background compatibility of \cref{sec:model-background-comparison,sec:two-sided-model-backgrounds}, including higher-dimensional limits that lose bigness or positive lower volume.

formal_entries.label: qu:nef-degeneration-exponent
formal_entries.text:
\label{qu:nef-degeneration-exponent}
Which geometric conditions on a nonclosed nef background force a common degeneration order, or an integral one? When is equality attained in the modification and residual order comparisons?
formal_entries.state: Both orders lie in $[0,n]$ and are independent of $\mu$ and $h$, of positive scaling, and of smooth gauge. For closed nef backgrounds on a K\"ahler manifold they equal $n-\operatorname{nd}(\theta)$. Nonclosed examples on products of elliptic curves realize unequal orders, irrational common orders, and zero volume with decay slower than every positive power. A modification can strictly increase the orders; effective residual subtraction also gives a one-sided comparison. Explicit elliptic threefolds have integral orders determined by the rank of their boundary forms. The flat-torus criterion separates current rigidity from rank: a nonzero semipositive boundary class is rigid exactly when its kernel leaves are dense, equivalently when a fixed positive perturbation collapses in diameter (Book, Theorem~27.16.1, printed p.~1028). Irrational and rational kernel slopes give the two alternatives (Book, Example~27.16.1, printed p.~1029). Arbitrary approaching flat K\"ahler forms can collapse at a nonrigid limiting class (Book, Example~27.16.2, printed p.~1029). These metric distinctions do not supply the nonclosed degeneration-order conditions asked for here. A Kummer resolution also has a nonzero smooth semipositive, nonrigid irrational boundary class with square zero (Book, Proposition~27.17.1, printed p.~1031). A global periodic $\ddc$ primitive identifies the representatives' Bott--Chern classes, and two explicitly translated torus periods detect the irrational ray. The resolved surface contains sixteen exceptional curves (Book, Lemma~27.17.1, printed p.~1030); the example does not address the curve-free regime of P11.\par Book, Lemma~25.18.3, printed p.~825 proves a full-Gauduchon-infimum comparison when $\theta\leq CB$ and $\theta+\ddc\varphi\geq cB$, with $\varphi\in L^1$, $c,C>0$, and $B$ closed semipositive on a compact K\"ahler manifold. Constant rank $R$ gives two-sided variational-volume bounds by $\epsilon^{n-R}$ for arbitrary smooth positive probability and Hermitian perturbation. Theorem~25.18.1, printed p.~827 constructs such a comparison for products of projective spaces and their linear-center blowups. The fixed cone has nonnegative parameters in $\theta=\sum_i((a_i+b_if_i)H_i+(c_i+d_ig_i)Q_i)$, with strictly positive fixed smooth $f_i,g_i$, omitted $Q_i$ terms on plain factors, and fixed pullback Fubini--Study generators. These functions may depend on every product coordinate. Each $H_i$-active block contributes $m_i$ to $R$, each $Q_i$-only blown block contributes $m_i-\ell_i-1$, and an inactive block contributes zero. All zero parameters and the zero background are included. An exceptional-divisor logarithm supplies the lower current bound; no restricted invariant/product test or Monge--Amp\`ere mass extremum replaces the variational infimum.\par Proposition~25.18.10, printed p.~828 preserves this order under every specified product linear blowup and, more generally, every modification with compact K\"ahler manifold source. In the latter case the book also proves two-sided power bounds, using the closed-background intersection polynomial after pulling back the actual nonzero divisor sections. The upstairs probability is independently smooth and positive; a degenerate pullback probability is not used in the smooth dual formula.\par Lemma~25.18.4, printed p.~829 determines the exact numerical range of the specified finite effective real sums of zero divisors of sections of integer tensor powers of the $H_i,Q_i$ bundles, with their fixed metrics: $\delta_i\geq0$ on plain factors and $\delta_i\geq0$, $\delta_i+\rho_i\geq0$ on blown factors. Theorem~25.18.2, printed p.~830 assumes the sufficient representation-preserving inequalities $a_i\geq\delta_i$, $c_i\geq\rho_i$. The residual remains in the same nef cone, its order gap is $\sum_i(R_i(\theta)-R_i(\beta))\geq0$, and equality holds exactly when every initially $H_i$-active block retains $a_i-\delta_i+b_i>0$ and every initially $Q_i$-only block retains $c_i-\rho_i+d_i>0$. Example~25.18.1, printed p.~830 gives genuinely nonclosed positive $\theta_t=tH+gQ$ and residual $(t-s)H+(g+s)Q$ after removal of $sE$, $0\leq s\leq t$. Equality holds for $s<t$, while $s=t$ gives jump $\ell+1$, realizing every integer from one to the dimension minus one. The chosen boundary current has actual divisorial mass, although perturbative minimal divisorial multiplicities remain zero.\par Book, Proposition~25.18.11, printed p.~831 removes the constant-rank requirement in this comparison. For a smooth closed semipositive $B$, put $R=\max_X\operatorname{rank}B$. The full quotient comparison and closed intersection polynomial give the same two-sided $\epsilon^{n-R}$ bounds: $B^{R+1}=0$, and the top nonzero mixed coefficient is positive on a nonempty open set. The target background is still nef, the ambient manifold is K\"ahler, and the lower comparison still requires its global $L^1$ potential. Corollary~25.18.2, printed p.~832 applies to any finite collection of smooth closed semipositive generators $B_j$ with fixed strictly positive smooth $f_j$ and parameters $t_j\geq0$: $\theta=\sum_jt_jf_jB_j$. Its order is $n-\max_X\operatorname{rank}(\sum_{t_j>0}B_j)$, including the empty active set. It preserves this order and the power bounds under every modification with compact K\"ahler manifold source, using only smooth pulled-back comparisons. The actual rank of the sum accounts for overlapping generators; constants are not asserted uniform across parameter faces. Example~25.18.2, printed p.~832 gives nonclosed $(f\circ p_2)p_1^*(b\omega_1)$ on $\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^q$, with $f>0$ nonconstant, $b\geq0$ nonzero and zero on an open set, and exact order $q$. Thus the closed generators themselves may have open zero-rank regions.\par A smooth compact connected anticanonical curve $D$ with $D^2=0$ in a complex surface has a unitary flat divisor line on a neighborhood (Book, Theorem~25.18.3, printed p.~835). The complete local proof uses a holonomy-independent flat elliptic inverse and a weighted fiberwise contraction; no arithmetic condition on the degree-zero normal line is imposed. A concave logarithmic cutoff gives a smooth closed semipositive divisor curvature $B$, supported in an annulus, of rank at most one (Book, Proposition~25.18.12, printed p.~837). On a compact K"ahler surface its maximum rank is exactly one, because $\int_SB\wedge\kappa=\int_D\kappa>0$. Every fixed smooth $f>0$ therefore gives a nef background $fB$ with two-sided variational-volume bounds by $\epsilon$ for arbitrary Hermitian perturbation and smooth positive probability; choices with $\mathrm df\wedge B\ne0$ are nonclosed (Book, Corollary~25.18.3, printed p.~838). For the closed perturbation, $\mathcal V_\mu(B+\epsilon\kappa)=2\epsilon\int_D\kappa+\epsilon^2\int_S\kappa^2$. Nine successive blowups along the strict transforms of a smooth plane cubic, including infinitely near centers, give these anticanonical square-zero curves (Book, Proposition~25.18.13, printed p.~838). The anticanonical line is semiample exactly when its elliptic normal line is torsion; exact order $m$ gives the first moving, basepoint-free system $|mD|$. For a non-torsion normal line every $|kD|$ is the singleton $\{kD\}$, yet the smooth rank-one semipositive curvature and nonclosed order-one multiples still exist. Thus the comparison class includes geometric generators that have no generated positive tensor power.\par The flat neighborhood also controls the divisor complement. For a smooth compact connected divisor in a complex manifold of dimension at least two, a flat divisor line gives compact Levi-flat circle levels. A torsion normal line of exact order $m$ gives a proper local holomorphic function with divisor $mD$ and connected compact nonzero fibers (Book, Proposition~25.18.14, printed p.~840). A non-torsion normal line has dense Levi leaves; maximum modulus forces every holomorphic function on a punctured tube to be constant. Thus every compact-hole complement that is connected has only constant holomorphic functions, which extend to the full divisor complement (Book, Theorem~25.18.4, printed p.~840). For either holonomy regime the complement is not Stein; in particular the non-torsion nine-point cubic example has the Hartogs property and only constant global holomorphic functions (Book, Corollary~25.18.4, printed p.~841). These complement results retain the flat-neighborhood hypothesis and do not supply a comparator for a general nonclosed nef background.
formal_entries.gap: No unrestricted common-order or integrality assertion survives the examples. Find hypotheses on geometry, torsion, or the degenerating positive representatives that force the closed-type behavior, and characterize equality in the comparison inequalities. These results fix strictly positive coefficient functions and specified closed semipositive generators or global current comparisons. Their divisor inequalities are sufficient for the displayed residual representation and do not characterize every nef residual or alternative cone representation. Fixed functions that vanish and modifications with non-Kahler source remain outside the proved regime. The maximum-rank criterion also requires a closed semipositive comparator and its stated global current comparison. It does not classify backgrounds without such a comparator or arbitrary vanishing coefficient functions. The generator corollary pulls back only smooth comparisons, so it makes no assertion about pulling back a general $L^1$ potential. The flat-divisor construction adds a geometric family within this comparison criterion; it does not provide a comparator for an arbitrary nonclosed nef background or classify all compact complex surfaces.

A compact complex manifold with $c_1^{\mathrm{BC}}(X)=0$ that admits a strictly LCK metric admits a Vaisman metric.

formal_entries.label: qu:hermitian-i-characterization
formal_entries.text:
\label{qu:hermitian-i-characterization}
For a big nonclosed background on a manifold with bounded mass, find criteria for $\underline{\operatorname{vol}}_\theta(P_\theta[u]_{\mathcal I})>0$ in terms of restricted multiplier ideals or divisorial orders. When this lower volume vanishes, which implications between envelope equality and upper-volume equality in \cref{prop:conditional-i-characterization} remain valid?

formal_entries.label: qu:individual-equation-threshold
formal_entries.text:
\label{qu:individual-equation-threshold}\index{Subsolution!exact threshold equation problem}
Suppose $v_-(h)=0$. For a nonzero $0\leq f\in L^1(\mathrm{d}V)$ with $b_h(f)>0$, does there exist $u\in\PSH(X,h)$ such that
\[
 \mathrm{MA}^{\mathrm{ext}}_h(u)=b_h(f)f\,\mathrm{d}V?
\]
Determine the singularity or envelope class in which such an equation should be posed.

formal_entries.label: thm:radial-positive-volume-nonbig
formal_entries.text:
\label{conj:nef-gaud-volume-big}\index{Gauduchon variational volume!bigness conjecture}
Let $\theta$ be a nef smooth real $(1,1)$-background on a compact complex manifold. Then
\[
 \mathcal V_\mu(\theta)>0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \theta\text{ is big}.
\]
Here $\mu$ is any smooth strictly positive probability measure.
formal_entries.current_resolution: resolved negatively in original unrestricted scope; counterexamples for n>=3
formal_entries.state: The unrestricted original equivalence is false. Book, Theorem~25.12.1, printed p.~784 constructs, for every $n\geq3$, a smooth semipositive nef nonclosed background on $\mathbb P^{n-1}\times\mathbb P^1$ that is not big and has $\mathcal V_\mu(\theta)=n$. Put $m=n-1$, $t=(m-1)/m$, $x=\sum_{j=1}^m|Z_j|^2/\sum_{j=0}^m|Z_j|^2$, $a=x/t$ and $\theta=\omega+a w$, with normalized Fubini--Study forms and $\mu=\omega^m\wedge w$. Book, Lemma~25.12.1, printed p.~782 gives the global bounded canonical radial potential by uniform smooth approximation, including the finite zero and every infinity chart. Its off-fiber determinant gives a lower bound against every smooth positive Gauduchon test; explicit smooth balanced metrics attain the matching perturbed quotients. A localized closed base-top-degree test excludes every strict quasi-psh current representative. Bigness still implies positive root volume. In dimension one the converse is the integral criterion; for closed nef classes on compact K\"ahler manifolds it is the classical nef-and-big criterion. The closed positive-volume core remains a sufficient condition. Positivity is independent of the chosen smooth positive probability. The result is independently reconstructed from the author's supplied source; it is not a priority or classification claim.
formal_entries.gap: No unresolved part of the original unrestricted equivalence remains: its forward implication is proved and its reverse implication is false. Separate followups concern nef nonclosed surface backgrounds, closed nef classes on general compact complex manifolds (P09), additional geometric criteria. P12 realizes the radial background, up to a smooth gauge change, at the maximal time of an actual Chern--Ricci flow and refutes that proposed endpoint implication too. Taking an infimum over all smooth probability densities would change the invariant and does not repair the original conjecture.

formal_entries.label: qu:closed-nef-gaud-bridge
formal_entries.text:
\label{qu:closed-nef-gaud-bridge}
Let $\alpha$ be closed and nef with $\int_X\alpha^n>0$. Prove a positive lower bound for $\lambda_\mu(\alpha)$, and rule out the collapse in \cref{prop:gaud-positive-volume-collapse} for a sequence minimizing the bigness threshold of $\alpha$.
formal_entries.state: Both bridges hold on compact K\"ahler manifolds. Guedj--Lu prove, under the stated nefness and positive intersection assumptions, bigness if and only if bounded upper mass holds. The book describes collapse of determinant denominators along threshold-minimizing Gauduchon tests. Neither its Hopf BMP counterexample nor its zero-lower-mass elliptic threefold provides a counterexample to the classical conjecture: neither carries the required closed nef class with positive top intersection. The radial counterexample resolving P08 has a nonclosed background and leaves both closed bridges separate.
formal_entries.gap: Prove a strictly positive Gauduchon root-volume bound from the closed intersection, then control the determinant denominator along at least one sequence minimizing the strict-current threshold. Prescribing a volume within an Aeppli class preserves the closed numerator but does not control trace normalization and denominator together.

formal_entries.label: qu:geometric-gaud-endpoint
formal_entries.text:
\label{qu:geometric-gaud-endpoint}
Find geometric conditions beyond the metric identities in \cref{cor:geometric-determinant-bound} that imply the endpoint estimate in \eqref{eq:pvp-endpoint-geometric}, and identify how they exclude the lower-mass degeneration of \cref{sec:vanishing-lower-mass}.
formal_entries.state:
The manuscript proves the exact equivalence
\[v_-(h)>0\ \Longleftrightarrow\ \sup_{T\in\mathscr G_h}\|k_T\|_{L^{n/(n-1)}(\mathrm dV)}<\infty,\quad
 \sup\|k_T\|_{n/(n-1)}=v_-(h)^{-1/n}.\]
Every strictly smaller exponent is uniformly controlled on arbitrary compact complex manifolds. The endpoint holds if a metric's first two powers are $\ddc$-closed, including K\"ahler manifolds and compact complex surfaces. A balanced BMP threefold has zero lower mass and violates the endpoint even for smooth positive tests. Theorem~25.15.1, printed p.~795, gives a geometric sufficient condition for principal elliptic threefolds over K\"ahler surfaces: the sum of the squares of the real curvature forms is nonnegative and nonzero. The bounded cubic identity gives the exact positive lower mass of the split metric and the endpoint for the full normalized current family in every Hermitian background. These manifolds have no pluriclosed metric. Proposition~25.15.2, printed p.~796, constructs negative-line-bundle quotients with nonzero second real cohomology; Proposition~25.15.3, printed p.~797, constructs a Calabi--Eckmann family without LCK metrics. Proposition~25.15.1, printed p.~796, identifies the opposite sign for primitive curvature pairs.
formal_entries.gap: The nonnegative curvature-pair criterion settles the stated principal elliptic threefold families. Find further geometric conditions, including changing-sign curvature, primitive elliptic bundles and higher-dimensional geometries. Balancedness plus BMP is insufficient. A bounded determinant density for one smooth maximizer gives no bound for all tests or all near-maximizing sequences.

formal_entries.label: prob:primitive-elliptic-lower-mass
formal_entries.text:
\label{prob:primitive-elliptic-lower-mass}
Determine the lower Monge--Amp\`ere mass of the primitive elliptic bundles
above, in particular those of \cref{ex:primitive-elliptic-k3}.
Does it vanish whenever the real Chern class is nonzero?

formal_entries.label: thm:actual-flow-positive-volume-nonbig
formal_entries.text:
\label{qu:chern-ricci-gaud-singularities}
Suppose a Chern--Ricci flow has finite maximal time $\tau$ and $\mathcal V_\mu(\theta_\tau)>0$. Can one prove that $\theta_\tau$ is big and that the flow converges smoothly to a positive metric locally on $X\setminus E_{\mathrm{nH}}(\theta_\tau)$, without a bounded mass hypothesis? How do the annihilating Gauduchon currents describe the resulting degeneracy?
formal_entries.state: The original first implication is false. Book, Theorem~25.19.3, printed p.~858 constructs an actual smooth Chern--Ricci flow on $\mathbb P^{n-1}\times\mathbb P^1$, for every $n\geq3$, with finite maximal book time $\tau=1/(2\pi)$ and a nef nonbig limiting background of exact fixed-density volume $n$. With the radial notation of P08, take $\omega_0=(n+1)\omega+(a+2)w$. Its endpoint is $\theta+\ddc\log(a+2)$, so smooth gauge invariance transfers the full Gauduchon volume and all-potential nonbigness obstruction. Strict reference representatives exist at every earlier time, and a closed base-top-degree test excludes even pseudoeffectivity at later times; the book's maximal-time theorem supplies the actual flow. Book, Proposition~25.19.2, printed p.~858 shows that every normalized endpoint annihilator has trace supported on $Z=\{p\}\times\mathbb P^1$ and vertical rank-one matrix. The explicit current is $[Z]/2$, and each annihilator satisfies $\int_X\omega(s)\wedge R=1-2\pi s$. This is an averaged trace, not pointwise metric collapse. Dang's qualitative null-locus equality and parabolic convergence theorem retain their nef-big or big endpoint hypotheses. The separate flow theorem using positive limiting lower volume retains the surface or Guan--Li assumptions.
formal_entries.gap: The unrestricted bigness implication is settled negatively, so the original proposed general conclusion cannot hold. Further directions concern additional conditions ensuring a big endpoint, geometric degeneration of actual evolving metrics, and analytic support for annihilators at other endpoints. In this model support follows from strict positivity of the semipositive representative away from one fiber; determinant vanishing alone still gives no general support theorem. Conditional smooth convergence off a big endpoint's non-Hermitian locus remains available from the cited theorem. Metric completeness and simultaneous nefness/smoothing compatibility remain separate refinements of S13. No surface counterexample, weak continuation or unconditional local convergence is asserted.
formal_entries.current_resolution: Negatively resolved: actual nonbig positive-volume flow endpoint for every n>=3

formal_entries.label: qu:balanced-pluriclosed-program
formal_entries.text:
\label{qu:balanced-pluriclosed-program}
Use the coexistence of a balanced metric and a pluriclosed metric to construct closed positive data, or to control a geometric flow that can change the torsion. Determine what estimate beyond the finite balanced trace prevents metric degeneration. Can determinant estimates for Gauduchon currents contribute to that estimate?

formal_entries.label: qu:hermitian-morse-program
formal_entries.text:
\label{qu:hermitian-morse-program}
Find geometric hypotheses controlling the cost in \eqref{eq:gaud-volume-subtraction-cost} up to a nef endpoint beyond the closed-core regime of \cref{thm:closed-core-subtraction}. Determine when positive root volume forces bigness without that core. For closed backgrounds, compare the estimate with classical Morse inequalities; for nonclosed backgrounds, retain the differential data and the dependence on $\mu$.
formal_entries.state: First variation proves the identity on positive compact segments without an upper mass bound. A closed nef positive-volume core plus a semipositive summand gives an endpoint estimate and a strict current. In the closed K\"ahler setting, the cited transcendental Morse inequality bounds the usual class volume by $\int\alpha^n-n\int\alpha^{n-1}\beta$; volume differentiability and cone duality are retained as literature inputs.
formal_entries.gap: Control the cost near arbitrary nef endpoints without the closed core and obtain a criterion making positive root volume imply bigness. For nonclosed forms, ordinary intersection expressions need not be invariant under smooth gauge. An estimate must specify its volume, retain torsion terms such as $\ddc$ of the added form, and state its dependence on $\mu$. The negative P08 resolution rules out an unconditional positive-volume bigness criterion for nef nonclosed backgrounds in dimension at least three; a geometric criterion must exclude that obstruction.

formal_entries.label: qu:gaud-metric-boundary
formal_entries.text:
\label{qu:gaud-metric-boundary}
For a specified finite-dimensional cone of smooth background classes, describe the metric completion of its unit-volume hypersurface. Which boundary points admit a current representative, and what estimates on the minimizing Gauduchon metrics distinguish finite from infinite distance?
formal_entries.status: partially resolved for invariant and warped background cones; general question open
formal_entries.state: Homogeneity gives an isometry $(\mathscr C,g)\simeq(\mathbb R\times\mathscr S,\mathrm dr^2+g_{\mathscr S})$ with $r=\log\lambda$. Thus paths with volume tending to zero or infinity have infinite length. The product cone on $\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^1$ is complete; the blowup of $\mathbb P^2$ has a finite-distance positive-nef-volume boundary. For a compact complex Lie-group quotient, a normalized invariant probability and a fixed real linear subspace $W\subset\operatorname{Herm}(n)$ containing a positive matrix, Book, Theorem~25.5.1, printed p.~723 proves that $\mathscr S=\{A>0:H\det A=1\}$ is complete and proper. Its Cauchy sequences are exactly coefficient sequences converging to a positive matrix. Book, Proposition~25.5.2, printed p.~720 identifies the normalized minimizing form as $\gamma_A=\theta_A/(H\det A)^{1/n}$ and characterizes positive-current coefficient classes by $A\geq0$. Spectral bounds control $\gamma_A$ pointwise. A nonzero singular coefficient limit becomes infinitely distant after normalization. In the full Iwasawa cone, Book, Example~25.5.2, printed p.~725 gives the exact logarithmic matrix distance and the explicit rate $\sqrt2|\log\varepsilon|/3$ for $\operatorname{diag}(1,1,\varepsilon)$ after normalization. Book, Theorem~25.5.2, printed p.~728 extends the determinant formula and the same complete prescribed coefficient metric on the Iwasawa quotient to every smooth probability invariant along its central elliptic fibers. These are exactly the smooth probabilities maximizing the volume of each invariant positive background. The minimizing metric is obtained from a closed base equation for the Schur complement; its coefficient mean retains the spectral distance bounds, without a claimed pointwise order estimate for the varying form. Book, Proposition~25.5.3, printed p.~726 identifies the upper mass of every invariant threefold positive background as $H\det A$. Book, Corollary~25.5.1, printed p.~727 gives zero non-pluripolar top mass for all plurisubharmonic potentials of singular semipositive invariant coefficients in dimension three. Book, Theorem~25.5.3, printed p.~730 computes the full reciprocal-integral volume and actual balanced minimizers on the entire three-dimensional warped cone on a compact K\"ahler $m$-fold times a curve, with $m\geq2$ and its specified product probability. Book, Proposition~25.5.4, printed p.~731 gives global Euclidean unit-surface coordinates. Book, Lemma~25.5.2, printed p.~733 identifies its endpoint length with the reciprocal-coefficient trace variance of the minimizing tests: under finite disjoint two-sided power-stratum hypotheses, an end is finite exactly when its minimum real-codimension/vanishing-order ratio exceeds one. Book, Theorem~25.5.4, printed p.~734 classifies every Cauchy point as a closed strip, closed half-plane or complete plane. Each finite end has a smooth semipositive nef nonbig representative of full variational volume one, with nonbigness proved against all singular strict current representatives. Book, Example~25.5.3, printed p.~739 gives an explicit $\mathbb P^2$ product strip and Book, Example~25.5.4, printed p.~740 an explicit complete torus plane with periodic base potentials. \par Book, Proposition~25.5.5, printed p.~735 determines the full pseudoeffective, nef and strict-current cones in that same real span using localized closed tests on arbitrary quasi-plurisubharmonic current representatives. Book, Proposition~25.5.6, printed p.~735 gives a continuous pulled-back potential solving the smooth positive prescribed-volume equation at every finite power-stratum unit-volume face. The base reciprocal density is in $L^p$ for every $1<p<r$, where $r>1$ is the endpoint codimension-to-order ratio. The bounded product equals the fixed probability, but no solution is globally $C^{1,1}$: bounded coefficients and the positive determinant would force a strict current representative excluded by the cone test. The obstruction is the general determinant-to-current bound in Book, Proposition~1.7.3, printed p.~37. Book, Proposition~25.5.7, printed p.~736 proves uniform whole-sequence convergence of the constructed normalized pulled-back potentials to every finite unit-volume face, weak convergence of all their ordinary bounded products and uniqueness among normalized bounded solutions pulled back from the base. Strong reciprocal-density convergence supplies the fixed-background compactness bound; closed-base uniqueness identifies all cluster potentials. For an arbitrary bounded pulled-back endpoint competitor, closed mass invariance and positivity exclude residual mass on the extreme set before uniqueness is applied. Uniqueness among arbitrary endpoint solutions, smoothness off the real extreme strata and pointwise convergence of minimizing balanced metrics remain unproved. \par Book, Proposition~25.5.8, printed p.~738 gives the exact balanced-cofactor trace and its sharp threshold: for $r>2$ the whole cofactor sequence has a finite positive closed current limit; for $1<r<2$ its trace has order $\epsilon^{r-2}$, and for $r=2$ order $\log(1/\epsilon)$. Book, Proposition~25.5.9, printed p.~739 identifies every trace-normalized current cluster for $1<r\leq2$ as the pullback of a base probability supported on the extreme components with minimal codimension-to-order ratio. A single extreme point gives whole-sequence convergence to its curve-fiber integration current. The smooth numerator and denominator have the same vanishing rate, while their quotient remains one. In the projective strip both ends are in this logarithmic regime. These conclusions concern the fixed product probability and power-stratum geometry; they do not determine a pointwise metric limit or enlarge the general completion theorem.
formal_entries.gap: Classify the unit-volume completion for other specified background cones and reference densities, together with their current representatives and minimizing-metric estimates. The general Lie-group result uses the invariant probability, while the larger fiber-invariant density family is proved specifically on the Iwasawa quotient. Densities varying along its central fibers have strictly smaller variational volume; their Hessian completion is not determined by that value inequality. Nonzero singular coefficient limits in the proved matrix families are infinitely distant after normalization, while a raw sequence tending to zero may normalize to an existing positive point. Adjoining all nef classes does not give the answer. Distances may shorten after enlarging the cone; no infinite-dimensional completion follows. The warped completion theorem fixes its product probability and excludes intersecting extreme strata and infinite-order zeros. Trace-moment estimates do not assert a pointwise limit of the minimizing metrics. Completion for other warped densities and extreme-set geometries remains open.

formal_entries.label: conj:continuous-gaud-adjoint
formal_entries.text:
\label{conj:continuous-gaud-adjoint}\index{Adjoint measure!continuous-density conjecture}
For a Hermitian background $\omega$, the nonsingular reference $\varphi=0$, and every real $F\in C(X)$, the set $\mathcal A_0(F)$ consists of a single probability measure.

formal_entries.label: qu:singularity-topology-program
formal_entries.text:
\label{qu:singularity-topology-program}\index{Singularity type!topology problem}
Extend the complete metrizable topology of \cref{thm:positive-model-complete-metric} on ordinary models beyond bounded mass and positive lower volume, retaining analytic closure exactly at the ideal models. Preserve the smooth-gauge and two-sided background compatibility of \cref{sec:model-background-comparison,sec:two-sided-model-backgrounds}, and treat background limits losing bigness or a uniform positive lower-volume bound. Recover the complete polar-variation topology of \cref{cor:curve-model-completeness} on all curve models, and determine whether the higher-dimensional extension is completely metrizable.

formal_entries.label: qu:exact-trace-program
formal_entries.text:
\label{qu:exact-trace-program}
If $Y$ fails at least one of the two mass properties, can the Hermitian background $\Omega$ in \cref{thm:trace-profile-model-envelope} be chosen so that
\[
 \nu\bigl(\mathcal T_\Omega(u;Y)\circ\pi,E\bigr)
       =\tau_{Y,u}(E)
\]
for every prime divisor $E$ on every smooth modification $\pi$ of $Y$? If so, determine a background-compatible ordinary or ideal singularity class of this realization, and prove its addition and approximation properties.

formal_entries.label: qu:positive-system-recovery
formal_entries.text:
\label{qu:positive-system-recovery}
For a smooth big background on a manifold without bounded mass, find a condition on a compatible Hermitian envelope system that forces recovery of its ideal type at every finite parameter. It should recover the positive limiting lower-volume criterion of \cref{thm:positive-volume-system-recovery} when bounded mass holds. Specify the invariant and uniform estimates that replace the finite upper-volume deficit, and their behavior under modifications.

formal_entries.label: qu:partial-kernel-lower-program
formal_entries.text:
\label{qu:partial-kernel-lower-program}
Identify hypotheses on a weighted section series and its intrinsic growth dimension under which the partial Fubini--Study potentials attain the envelope lower bound and the normalized kernel measures converge. Relate the limiting measure to the Hermitian background while retaining the closed curvature and the growth dimension of the series.
formal_entries.state: The general upper-envelope bound is proved. A matching lower bound and kernel-measure convergence hold in the closed-curvature positive-mass setting with a K\"ahler modification, retaining its Jacobian and relative canonical bundle. Descended series on submersions give base-dimensional limits. Isolated-point conditions permit finite-codimension comparison; horizontal projective and explicit Hopf series give further exact limits. Hopf growth has degree $n-1$, so normalization by $m^n$ would discard its nonzero limit. An interior rational Newton polytope on a product of projective lines gives a complete sufficient-condition model when its affine hull has an integral offset, its smooth invariant logarithmic weight is strictly convex, and its sampling probability is smooth, strictly positive and invariant on the whole manifold. Book, Theorem~26.16.1, printed p.~957 proves the specified growth-envelope lower bound, all finite $L^p$ convergence and weighted Bernstein--Markov. Book, Theorem~26.16.2, printed p.~959 computes the positive relative-dimensional kernel limit as lattice volume lifted to real moment tori. It is independent of the invariant sampling probability. In lower dimension it is singular and differs from the ambient mixed envelope-curvature measure; in full dimension it equals the non-pluripolar top product. Book, Example~26.16.1, printed p.~960 includes nonclosed smooth sampling and a rational map with indeterminacy. A critical divisor multiplier-ideal family on a product of projective lines has positive growth exponent $q$ and potentials converging to its actual ideal envelope, while its $q!m^{-q}$-normalized kernel measures have two different positive weak limits. Book, Theorem~26.17.1, printed p.~961 computes $N_m=a_m(m+1)^q$, with $a_m=1$ in even and $2$ in odd degrees, and restores a single probability limit after division by $N_m$. Its selector has zero top non-pluripolar mass and its ideal family is not multiplicative. This shows that a growth exponent alone is insufficient outside the positive-mass convergence regime.\par An actual ideal selector at the two isolated base points of a pencil on $\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^1$ gives a convergent non-multiplicative model. Book, Lemma~26.18.1, printed p.~964 identifies its all-weight ideal and ordinary upper type classes for every genuine competitor. Theorem~26.18.1, printed p.~966 computes the full ideal envelope for the specified compact logarithmic box and quadratic norm weight. Proposition~26.18.1, printed p.~967 gives the entire three-band space and exact dimension $3m+1$. Theorem~26.18.2, printed p.~968 proves a global potential lower bound, every finite $L^p$ convergence, uniform exponential convergence and an intrinsic positive measure limit of mass three. Additive error remains unbounded near each pole at every fixed degree $m\geq2$. The norm, box and sampling probability are fixed; this selector also has zero top non-pluripolar mass.
formal_entries.gap: Find intrinsic hypotheses producing enough sections with the full ideal constraints and controlling their measures. The Newton theorem specifies a growth-constrained target; it does not identify an arbitrary multiplier-ideal envelope. Boundary-touching polytopes, noninvariant data and general selected series remain outside its hypotheses. Preserve closed line-bundle curvature while relating the limit to a possibly nonclosed ambient background. No unqualified equality with the raw Hermitian Monge--Amp\`ere measure of the selecting weight follows from the upper bound. Require convergence of the normalized section counts for a finite weak kernel-measure limit, rather than merely an intrinsic growth exponent. The specific three-band pencil model does not establish a universal all-weight ideal/ordinary class identity or convergence for other compact sampling and arbitrary selected families.

formal_entries.label: qu:fiber-selected-approximation
formal_entries.text:
\label{qu:fiber-selected-approximation}
Let $\pi:X\to B$ be a surjective holomorphic submersion of connected compact complex manifolds with connected fibers, where $B$ is K\"ahler of dimension $q\geq1$. Fix a Hermitian form $\omega$ on $X$, a holomorphic line bundle $A$ with a smooth Hermitian metric $h$ on $B$, and $\varphi\in\PSH(X,\omega)$. Set $\theta=c_1(A,h)$. For positive integers $m$, identify
\[
 V_m=H^0\bigl(X,\pi^*A^m\otimes\mathcal I(m\varphi)\bigr)
          \subseteq H^0(B,A^m)
\]
by holomorphic descent. Find geometric or analytic conditions that produce $\psi\in\PSH(B,\theta)$ of positive non-pluripolar mass such that, for all sufficiently large $m$,
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 W_m=H^0\bigl(B,A^m\otimes\mathcal I(m\psi)\bigr)\subseteq V_m,\\
 \dim V_m-\dim W_m=o(m^q).
 \end{gathered}
\]
Determine which features of the singularities of $\varphi$ along the fibers suffice for this approximation.

formal_entries.label: prob:growing-jets-localization
formal_entries.text:
\label{prob:growing-jets-localization}
Let $C$ be a connected compact Riemann surface, let $x\in C$, and let $(L,h)$ be a smooth Hermitian holomorphic line bundle whose curvature is semipositive and strictly positive on $C\setminus\{x\}$. Fix an integer $r\geq1$. Suppose that in a local coordinate $z$ centered at $x$ and a holomorphic frame $e$ one has
\[
 |e|_h^2=\mathrm{e}^{-\phi},\qquad
 \phi(z)=|z|^{2r}+O(|z|^{2r+1}).
\]
Let $\nu$ be a smooth positive volume form with local expression $a(z)\,\mathrm{d}A$ and $a(0)=1$, where $\mathrm{d}A$ is Euclidean area. For positive integers $m$, choose integers $q_m\to\infty$ with $q_m=o(m)$. Give
\[
 V_m=H^0(C,L^m\otimes\mathfrak m_x^{q_m})
\]
the norm $\|s\|^2=\int_C|s|_{h^m}^2\,\mathrm{d}\nu$, where $\mathfrak m_x$ is the ideal sheaf of $x$. Write $B_m=\sum_j|s_{m,j}|_{h^m}^2$ for an orthonormal basis $(s_{m,j})$ of $V_m$, with value zero when $V_m=0$. Determine the growth ranges of $q_m$ for which, for each fixed real $\tau$, every sequence of points $x_m$ in the coordinate neighborhood satisfying
\[
 m|z(x_m)|^{2r}=q_m/r+\tau\sqrt{q_m/r}
\]
obeys
\[
 \frac{\pi B_m(x_m)}{mr^2|z(x_m)|^{2r-2}}
 \longrightarrow
 \Phi(\tau):=\frac1{\sqrt{2\pi}}\int_{-\infty}^{\tau}
                         \mathrm{e}^{-s^2/2}\,\mathrm{d}s.
\]
When this transition law fails, determine how further terms of the local weight change its center and scale.

formal_entries.label: qu:singular-space-equations-program
formal_entries.text:
\label{qu:singular-space-equations-program}
Beyond the projective-cone constructions of \cref{sec:projective-cone-equations}, determine geometric and measure conditions on compact unibranch Hermitian spaces that give existence and uniqueness in specified singularity classes. Identify estimates ensuring finite mass, descent and continuity, and their behavior under common refinements.
formal_entries.state:
The appendix proves disk-test descent under modifications and compatibility of ordinary envelopes, constructs resolution-independent non-pluripolar products, and gives explicit equations on projective cones under stated inequalities on their data. Dang provides continuity for bounded solutions under additional hypotheses, notably a log-terminal setting. Pan constructs a Gauduchon metric on the regular locus uniformly comparable to the prescribed metric, with conformal uniqueness up to scale.
 In the explicitly assumed standard nodal small-resolution model, Book, Lemma~13.18.3 constructs a strict analytic barrier and Corollary~13.18.1 gives a bounded fixed-smooth-density equation by subsequential potential degeneration, with exact exceptional-area decay. Book, Lemma~13.18.4 computes the pushed-forward density: it is in $L^p$ precisely for $1\leq p<3$, has a weak $L^3$ endpoint and is not in $L^3$ when a node is present. The bounded potential descends, including for a nonclosed ambient background, and solves (Book, equation~13.52) on the singular space. When the pullback background is closed, Book, Theorem~13.18.2 proves uniqueness among bounded normalized solutions and convergence of the entire smooth perturbation family. These arguments do not establish continuity at a node or settle the general prescribed-class problem.\par For compact unibranch curves with finite bijective torus normalization, Book, Lemma~A.7.1, printed p.~1254 constructs a periodic Green function directly. Theorem~A.7.1, printed p.~1255 proves an equation in every prescribed finite logarithmic ordinary type of total pole weight $A<H$, for nonzero nonnegative normalization-side $L^p$ data with $p>1$. Here $H=\int_E\pi^*h$, $\beta_0$ is flat area probability on the normalization $E$, and $f\geq0$ is its data density. The proportionality constant is $(H-A)/\int f\beta_0$, the entire genuine type has mass $H-A$, and uniqueness includes initially rough competitors. Disk lifts give genuine descent, a continuous residual and extended-value continuity at the poles; all curve resolutions and refinements are biholomorphic to the normalization. The local-embedding background may pull back degenerately. Example~A.7.1, printed p.~1257 supplies a nonnormal projective cusp with genus-one normalization, background mass six and a weight-one pole of nonpluripolar mass five. Its normalization-side density is smooth and positive, but the downstairs density belongs to $L^r(h)$ exactly for $1\leq r<2$, with logarithmic divergence at $r=2$. This is a dimension-one sufficient condition; all curve backgrounds are closed.\par Book, Theorem~A.7.2, printed p.~1260 gives an exact endpoint for normalization-side densities with local form $C_0|z|^{-2}(\log(1/|z|))^{-\gamma}$, where $C_0>0$ and the density is smoothly and positively extended away from the chosen point. They are integrable exactly for $\gamma>1$ and lie outside every $L^p$, $p>1$. Within this family, a positive-proportionality equation has a solution in the prescribed ordinary logarithmic type exactly for $\gamma>2$; it is unique in that entire type and has a continuous residual with no positive H\"older exponent upstairs. For $1<\gamma\leq2$, a constructed genuine descended solution has the same mass $H-A$ and all-weight resolution multiplier ideals, but its residual is unbounded below. No ordinary-type solution exists, even with an unspecified positive proportionality constant. The proof uses a cutoff radial primitive and a smooth mean-zero Green correction; it retains the possibly degenerate background.\par In every dimension $n\geq2$, an explicit product of a cuspidal curve with square elliptic curves has a nonclosed local-embedding Hermitian background whose normalization admits a positive smooth reference repair and has all background powers $\mathrm{dd}^{\mathrm c}$-closed (Book, Proposition~A.8.1, printed p.~1262). Fix an integer $s\geq n+3$ before choosing its sufficiently small nonzero real perturbation. A quantitative contraction solves full-variable normalized densities in a small $H^s$ neighborhood of the positive reference density, with a $C^2$ normalization-side potential and solution form at least one quarter of the flat reference (Book, Theorem~A.8.1, printed p.~1263). Every bounded ordinary potential has the same mass, and a weighted decreasing-product limit gives uniqueness against all bounded competitors, including rough ones (Book, Lemma~A.8.1, printed p.~1264; Proposition~A.8.2, printed p.~1264). The normalized potential descends genuinely, is ambient H\"older of exponent $1/3$, has forced scalar $c=M/\nu(X)$, and solves the equation on every resolution and common refinement. The datum gives the cusp locus zero mass; near it the exact downstairs density is $\lambda f/\rho$, with $\rho=4|z|^2+9|z|^4$ (Book, Theorem~A.8.2, printed p.~1265). Separately, the existing bounded-mass theorem on the positive repaired normalization gives bounded existence for every nonzero nonnegative normalization-side $L^p$ density, $p>1$, without the smallness condition (Book, Corollary~A.8.1, printed p.~1267). Regularity and entire bounded-class uniqueness are established here for the small Sobolev regime. The original general problem remains open.
formal_entries.gap: Find assumptions giving finite mass, existence, uniqueness in the specified class, and continuity downstairs, stable under common refinements. Arbitrary unibranch singularities are not covered by log-terminal results. Scalar bounds and resolution-level regularity do not alone supply descent or control near the singular locus. Torus normalization, finitely many logarithmic poles and normalization-side integrability are fixed hypotheses. The curve theorem gives no criterion for arbitrary singularity types or higher-dimensional nonclosed backgrounds. A criterion for arbitrary integrable normalization-side data remains open. The explicit endpoint construction does not prove a mass or uniqueness theorem for the whole resolution-ideal class.
